newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian MinFins rise on Paris Club news.
newsitem.headline: Russian MinFins rise on Paris Club news.

text.p: Prices of Russian MinFin bonds rose on news Russia would join the Paris Club of creditor countries, dealers said on Monday, adding the bonds were also tracking firmer U.S. Treasury bills.
"Prices rose 0.5 point in the morning on the positive (Paris Club) news," an International Moscow Bank dealer said.
The Paris Club said in a statement late on Friday that its chairman, Christian Noyer, had on Friday reached an understanding with Russian Deputy Finance Minister Mikhail Kasyanov.
"Firmer U.S. Treasuries is another supporting factor," one dealer said.
MinFins, like other emerging debt, are sensitive to any news which would suggest a change in U.S. interest rates and consequently affect U.S. Treasury bond prices.
Dealers said Western banks were taking profit at current levels on the fourth, fifth and sixth tranches but local banks were buying the paper.
They added London demand for the seventh tranche was noticed as well.
